effect: The result completes Augustine’s account: both infants inherit the condition regardless of health, while neither has personally chosen wrongdoing. It also notes that Christians dispute the teaching.
reaction: The distinction between illness and personal wrongdoing was helpful, as was acknowledging disagreement.

mostWorthwhile.text: Applying the inherited-condition claim to both infants was most worthwhile: it clarified the argument without treating illness as evidence of guilt.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial pairing of knowing right with choosing otherwise felt fairly predictable, although it set up the grace argument.

surprise.text: The baptism result distinguished a practice that raises a question from proof of Augustine’s answer; that sharpened how I understood the argument.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the final two combinations were the only offered actions rather than discoveries of compatibility.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how later arguments reuse these distinctions, especially given the careful separation of claims from evidence.
